Then reason: the original tower is numbered from bottom to top as 1 to 90. Grouped every three blocks, they are (1,2,3), (4,5,6), ..., (37,38,39), (40,41,42), ..., (88,89,90). Each time Bob takes three blocks from the top of the old tower, so the order of the three-block groups in the new tower is opposite to the original order of the three-block groups, but within each group the order from bottom to top is still maintained. For example, near 39 and 40, the two adjacent groups in the original tower are (37,38,39) and (40,41,42). In the new tower, the group (40,41,42) will be below (37,38,39). Therefore this section in the new tower from bottom to top is 40, 41, 42, 37, 38, 39. The blocks located between 40 and 39 are 41, 42, 37, 38, a total of 4 blocks.

method.method_draft: Use a position formula instead of listing the tower. From the image, first read that Bob is not individually reversing the three blocks: each three-block stack is transferred intact, so the relative order inside each triple is preserved while the sequence of triples is reversed. From the text, labels run from 1 at the bottom to 90 at the top, so there are 30 triples. For a block numbered n, let g = ceil(n/3) be its original triple counted from the bottom: triple 1 is 1,2,3; triple 30 is 88,89,90. In the new tower, triple g is the (31-g)-th triple from the bottom. The position from the bottom of n is therefore 3(30-g)+r, where r is its position inside its triple. For 40, g=14 and r=1, so its new position is 3(16)+1=49. For 39, g=13 and r=3, so its new position is 3(17)+3=54. The number of blocks between them is 54-49-1=4.
